svg.text: What a stool exam panel checks for
A doctor picks the test, or combination, based on the symptoms being investigated.
Ova and parasites (O&P)
Eggs, larvae or adult worms under a microscope
Detects hookworm, roundworm, tapeworm, giardia
Often needs 2 to 3 samples on different days
Ordered for: chronic diarrhoea, suspected worms
Occult (hidden) blood
Chemical or immunochemical test (FIT/FOBT)
Finds blood invisible to the naked eye
A screening flag, not a diagnosis on its own
Ordered for: GI bleeding, colorectal cancer screening
Stool culture
Grows bacteria from the sample over a few days
Identifies Salmonella, Shigella, and similar bacteria
Can guide which antibiotic will work, if needed
Ordered for: bloody or persistent diarrhoea, fever
Stool antigen tests
Detects markers from a specific organism directly
Includes the H. pylori stool antigen test
Faster than culture, usually a day or two
Ordered for: suspected ulcer-causing infection
General guide, not a full list. Your doctor selects the test based on your symptoms and history.
